words.gloss: even if he does not have

literal: A king who does not have those who reprove him, being unprotected, will perish even if he has no one to destroy him.
translation: A king who lacks the guidance of those who can openly reprove his faults is unprotected and will ruin himself, even if he has no enemies to destroy him.
modern: தவறு செய்யும்போது கடிந்து அறிவுரை கூறும் பெரியோர்களைத் துணையாகக் கொள்ளாத, பாதுகாப்பற்ற மன்னன், தன்னை அழிக்கும் பகைவர் யாரும் இல்லாவிட்டாலும் தானே அழிந்துவிடுவான்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the vital role of wise counselors who have the courage to criticize and correct a ruler's mistakes. The word 'இடிப்பாரை' refers to those who reprove or admonish with harsh but necessary truths. A king without such guides is described as 'ஏமரா' (unprotected), meaning he lacks a defensive shield against his own errors. Even in the absence of external enemies ('கெடுப்பார் இலானும்'), his own unchecked missteps will inevitably lead to his downfall ('கெடும்'). Thus, honest criticism is presented not as a threat, but as an essential safeguard for leadership.
